waves.name: Batch brackets, GDG bases and utility definers
waves.rationale: Holds CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL, the two jobs that close and reopen the CICS files around every batch window, and the jobs that define the GDG bases posting, the report and the backup chain write into. This is not a family of jobs that touch no shared data. CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL act on the shared masters by console command, and DEFGDGB, DALYREJS and REPTFILE create the generation bases that POSTTRAN, TRANREPT and TRANBKP need before their first run. They are low effort and they prove the scheduler, the JCL translation and the GDG replacement. Six units the seed put here left for waves 5 and 7 (see deviations).
waves.unblocks: The batch window itself. Every job in waves 4 and 5 needs the close and open brackets and the GDG bases. CLOSEFIL and OPENFIL cannot be retired until wave 6 removes CICS ownership of the VSAM files.

waves.name: Read-only extract and print batch
waves.rationale: Programs and jobs that read the account, card, customer and cross reference masters and write only files nobody else reads. READACCT, READCARD, READCUST and READXREF print the masters, so they double as the read-back check for the master refresh in wave 4. CBIMPORT writes staging files no program in the tree reads, and reads what CBEXPORT (wave 5) writes, so it must accept files written by the legacy exporter.
waves.unblocks: The read path for every VSAM master and the shared record layouts CVACT01Y, CVACT02Y, CVACT03Y and CVCUS01Y. It also gives a print-and-compare harness that waves 4 and 5 reuse.

waves.name: Sign-on, menu and read-only online screens
waves.rationale: Seven online programs that read masters and write nothing. COSGN00C, COMEN01C and COADM01C are one strongly connected component and move together. COTRN00C and COTRN01C are another. The menu routes to later-wave programs through a table (COMEN02Y), so the facade must route XCTL by program name across the legacy and the new runtime until wave 6. CORPT00C and CSUTLDTC left this wave (see deviations).
waves.unblocks: The online shell: sign-on, menu and admin menu. Every later online wave plugs into it. It also proves the BMS to new-UI conversion on screens that cannot damage data.

waves.name: Master data loaders and reference data jobs
waves.rationale: The must-not-break 'account and card master refresh' lives here: ACCTFILE and CARDFILE (scripts/remote_refresh.sh:16-20) plus the other master and reference loaders (XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, TRANFILE, TCATBALF, DISCGRP, TRANTYPE, TRANCATG, DUSRSECJ). Their IDCAMS cards carry the record contract (KEYS, RECORDSIZE, alternate index offsets) that the extractor does not read, so the seed's 'writes are guesses' label is accurate. Eleven of the 29 units are mainframe build and test tooling (compile jobs, build procs, REPRTEST, SORTTEST) that are retired, not ported, which leaves 18 units to move. TRANBKP, COMBTRAN and TRANIDX, which the seed put here or in wave 1, moved to wave 5 because they share the transaction master lifecycle with posting. CARDFILE scores high-high and stays: it is one half of the must-not-break master refresh with ACCTFILE, and splitting that item across waves is worse than a high-high unit at the middle of the plan. Dependency wins over the quadrant.
waves.unblocks: Wave 5. The loaders are what let the seed data be reloaded before every posting and report test run, and the harness for waves 5 and 6 needs them.

waves.name: Daily posting, interest, transaction report and statements
waves.rationale: The batch cycle that holds two of the three must-not-break items: POSTTRAN with CBTRN02C (daily transaction posting) and the transaction report (TRANREPT, CBTRN03C, and its online trigger CORPT00C). It also holds interest (INTCALC, CBACT04C), the jobs that empty, rebuild and re-index the transaction master (TRANBKP, COMBTRAN, TRANIDX), statements (CREASTMT, CBSTM03A and B) and the export. It passes the four wave tests only if the VSAM masters are served through one data facade for legacy online and new batch, because ACCTDATA has four writers and TRANSACT has three across waves 5 and 6. Rollback needs a snapshot of ACCTDATA and TCATBALF taken before the run. The legacy cycle takes none: it backs up only the transaction master (TRANBKP) and reloads the account and category files from PS files (scripts/run_posting.sh:17-20), so the port has to add one to pass the rollback test. The boundary is the daily file in and the masters, DALYREJS and TRANREPT out. Several units score high-high and the wave is at the back of the plan, as intended.
waves.unblocks: Retires the batch half of the shared masters and the transaction master lifecycle (TRANBKP, POSTTRAN, INTCALC, COMBTRAN, TRANIDX). Leaves the online writers (wave 6) as the last users of the legacy VSAM store.

waves.name: Online writers: accounts, cards, bill payment, transactions, users
waves.rationale: The nine online programs that write the shared masters. COACTUPC (3,368 lines) and COBIL00C carry the highest blast radius in the online set. The card programs use CCARD-NEXT-PROG to chain COCRDLIC to COCRDSLC and COCRDUPC, so COCRDLIC (self recursive) moves with them.
waves.unblocks: Removes the last online writer of the VSAM masters, so the legacy VSAM store and the CICS regions can be retired for the in-tree application.

waves.name: IMS, DB2 and MQ subsystem
waves.rationale: Everything that touches DB2, IMS or MQ: the authorization module (COPAUA0C, COPAUS0C, COPAUS1C, COPAUS2C and the IMS batch programs), the DB2 transaction type maintenance (COTRTLIC, COTRTUPC, COBTUPDT and its jobs) and the two MQ programs. This plugin does not read DB2 DDL, IMS DBD or PSB, or MQ definitions, and 25 DB2 and IMS files (DCLGEN, DDL, DBD, PSB and control cards) are listed as not parsed, so this wave is the least certain. The seed put five DB2 jobs in wave 1 because their SQL is in in-stream cards. They are here now (see deviations).
waves.unblocks: Retirement of the mainframe. Also the weekly TRANTYPE and TRANCATG feed that the wave 5 report reads, and the CBPAUP0J job that CA-7 runs before POSTTRAN.

unassigned.reason: No job, CICS program definition or caller in the tree names it. Its DDs map to no JCL. It reads the daily file and masters but writes nothing. Kept out of the plan until telemetry shows whether it runs. See dead-code.json.

deviations.reason: Embedded JCL: CORPT00C builds a job that runs PROC=TRANREPT and writes it to the JOBS transient data queue. It is the online front of the transaction report, which the client says must not break. The seed called it read-only online because the extractor makes no edge for JCL text inside COBOL. It moves with the report job it launches. Cost: the wave 3 menu (COMEN01C) still routes to it through the option table, so the facade must route that XCTL to the legacy program until wave 5.

The seed rule moves a shared unit with the earliest family that uses it. With CORPT00C in wave 5, its callers are CORPT00C (wave 5), COACTUPC and COTRN02C (wave 6). Nothing in wave 3 calls it, so it moves to wave 5.

The proc that CORPT00C's embedded JCL executes (STEP10 EXEC PROC=TRANREPT). It holds the same sort and report steps as job:TRANREPT, so it moves with the report. It stays in the unknown dead-code bucket because a run-time submit is the only thing that reaches it.

IDCAMS control cards are not read by the extractor. TRANIDX defines and builds the alternate index over the shared transaction master (BLDINDEX on TRANSACT.VSAM.KSDS), and TRANBKP deletes that index every cycle. It runs after POSTTRAN and COMBTRAN in every wrapper, so it belongs to the posting cycle, not to utilities that touch no shared data.

risks.json scores it high-high (5 for blast radius: it empties the live transaction master). CBTRN02C opens that master OUTPUT, so POSTTRAN only works on the empty file TRANBKP leaves. TRANBKP, POSTTRAN, INTCALC and COMBTRAN share one file lifecycle in every wrapper. Wave 5 is the last wave that keeps that lifecycle inside one testable boundary, so it moves there.
risks.json scores it high-high. It rebuilds the transaction master from the TRANBKP generation and the INTCALC output (SYSTRAN), both wave 5 units. It moves with them.
A scheduler job moves with the job it runs. job:TRANBKP moves to wave 5.
A scheduler job moves with the job it runs. job:COMBTRAN moves to wave 5.

The step runs IKJEFT01 and the in-stream card RUN PROGRAM(COBTUPDT) PLAN(CARDDEMO), a DB2 batch program. In-stream control cards are not read, so the extractor saw a utility with no application program. It touches DB2, so it belongs to the subsystem family.
A scheduler job moves with the job it runs. job:MNTTRDB2 moves to wave 7.
Not unreachable. A weekly Control-M job runs MNTTRDB2, whose in-stream DSN card runs COBTUPDT. The extractor cannot see it, so it left the program unplaced. It moves with its job.
The steps run DSNTIAUL SQL against CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE and its category table in in-stream cards the extractor does not read. It touches DB2, so it belongs to the subsystem family.
A scheduler job moves with the job it runs. job:TRANEXTR moves to wave 7.

The steps run IKJEFT01 with the DB2 create-database, plan-free and table-load control members (DB2FREE, DB2TIAD1, DB2CREAT, DB2TEP41). Those members are in the not-parsed list. It touches DB2, so it belongs to the subsystem family.

Named in the PARM of the IMS batch driver DFSRRC00 in job CBPAUP0J, which the CA-7 listing triggers after CLOSEFIL. The extractor does not read PARM, so it left the program unplaced. It moves with its job.
Named in the PARM of DFSRRC00 in job UNLDGSAM. It moves with its job.
Named in the PARM of DFSRRC00 in job LOADPADB. It moves with its job.
Named in the PARM of DFSRRC00 in job UNLDPADB. It moves with its job.
